Its own exemplar set puts a 0.494 near-neutral D-1 in the COIL band (G16 0331, -110) and a 0.463 sell D-1 in the TREND band (G16 0401, -600). On the corrected basis 0609's 0.490 lands on the COIL exemplar, so 0610 is licensed to -100..-250, not to -450..-780. The old series (0.454) would have put it squarely on the TREND exemplar and I would have emitted roughly -550 instead of -130. what_the_two_sided_series_actually_says.consequence_2_ATTRIBUTION: On 0616 the accumulation arm's 'under a sub-0.50 sell tape' condition holds on the ORIGINAL series (0615 = 0.406) and FAILS on the two-sided series (0615 = 0.520). The big prints read 0.841. On the original basis that looks like classic accumulation - big prints buying against a selling crowd. On the corrected basis the crowd was buying too (0.520), so there is no divergence at all: it is simply a buy day. The SIGN is unchanged (up), but the MECHANISM the arm claims is absent, so I have attributed 0616's sign to flow.price_free_absorption_proxy plus the COT gate and explicitly NOT to structure.accumulation_arm_turn. Recording this so a merge does not bank the denominator fix as forward evidence for the accumulation arm.
what_the_two_sided_series_actually_says.consequence_3_NO_BLANKET_FLIP: On 0617 both bases agree (0.468 and 0.366, both sub-0.50), so the corrected series changes nothing there. The fix is not a systematic up-shift; it is a re-ordering. That is the honest version of the claim.
